newsitem.title: UK: PETsMART sees Pet City boosting revenues.
newsitem.headline: PETsMART sees Pet City boosting revenues.

text.p: U.S. pet store company PETsMART Inc said on Friday it expected its acquisition of Britain's Pet City Holdings Plc to help the combined group's revenues reach nearly $2.0 billion next year.
The Phoenix-based company had revenues of $1.08 billion for its fiscal 1995, which ended on January 28 of this year.
"PETsMART will approach almost two billion dollars in fiscal 1997 (ended in January 1998)," chief executive officer Mark Hansen told Reuters in an interview.
He added that Pet City would comprise about 10 percent of the group's combined revenues in fiscal 1997.
Hansen said he expected most of PETsMART's revenue growth to come from its store expansion, along with its businesses targeting veterinary hospitals and catalog sales.

PETsMART, which currently has a base of 311 stores in North America, planned to expand that number to 320 by the end of this fiscal year and build an additional 60-70 superstores by the end of fiscal 1997.
"So we'll finish next year with approximately 380 to 390 North American stores," he said.
This expansion will include branching into Canada, where PETsMART plans to open eight stores next week.
